purpose: Pin the first structural break beyond the Cycle-Plus-Triangles theorem. Triangle inner components are always 3-colourable together with the Hamiltonian cycle, whereas a C4 inner component has a binary diagonal-equality witness in every proper colouring. Give an exact diagonal-contraction reformulation for C4-only smooth graphs and freeze an explicit eight-vertex non-3-colourable C4 control, without overclaiming C4-only NP-completeness from a broader source theorem.

triangle_terminal.theorem: Cycle-Plus-Triangles: every 4-regular graph whose edge set is the disjoint union of a Hamiltonian cycle and pairwise vertex-disjoint triangles is 3-colourable (indeed 3-choosable in the Fleischner-Stiebitz result).
triangle_terminal.algorithmic_meaning: If every inner component has length three, the decision answer is unconditionally YES and a constructive proof/algorithm can return a colouring. This is a genuine positive terminal, not a heuristic.

c4_local_theorem.cycle: Let C4=(a,b,c,d,a) be properly coloured with three colours.
c4_local_theorem.name: C4_HAS_AN_EQUAL_COLOUR_DIAGONAL
c4_local_theorem.statement: Every proper 3-colouring of C4 satisfies a=c OR b=d.
c4_local_theorem.proof: If a!=c, then b is adjacent to both a and c and therefore must use the unique third colour. The same is true for d, so b=d. The alternative a=c already satisfies the disjunction.
c4_local_theorem.two_colour_overlap: When the C4 uses only two colours, both diagonal equalities hold. With all three colours, exactly one diagonal equality holds.

diagonal_contraction_carrier.input: A smooth 4-regular Hamiltonian graph whose inner components are C4s C_i=(a_i,b_i,c_i,d_i).
diagonal_contraction_carrier.witness: For each inner C4 choose one diagonal delta_i in {{a_i,c_i},{b_i,d_i}}.
diagonal_contraction_carrier.quotient: Contract the two vertices of every selected diagonal, retaining all original edge inequalities (parallel edges may be deduplicated; a loop makes that selection immediately infeasible).
diagonal_contraction_carrier.theorem: G is 3-colourable iff there exists a diagonal selection delta such that the quotient G/delta is 3-colourable.
proof: Forward: any proper colouring supplies at least one equal-colour diagonal in every C4 by C4_HAS_AN_EQUAL_COLOUR_DIAGONAL. Contracting those equal-colour pairs preserves that colouring on the quotient.

Backward: any proper colouring of the quotient lifts by giving both endpoints of each contracted diagonal the quotient colour. Every original edge survives as an inequality edge, so the lifted colouring is proper in G.
diagonal_contraction_carrier.meaning: A C4 component contributes a binary equality-contraction witness. The global difficulty is not local C4 colouring but coordinating linearly many diagonal choices through the Hamiltonian/tension constraints.

explicit_c4_failure_control.fact: The resulting simple 4-regular smooth graph is not 3-colourable. The checker exhausts all 3^8 colourings and also verifies that none of the four diagonal-selection quotients is 3-colourable.
explicit_c4_failure_control.consequence: The Cycle-Plus-Triangles universal-YES property fails already when inner triangles are replaced by C4s. This finite fact is separate from any asymptotic hardness claim.

source_backed_hard_boundary.literature: Fleischner-Sabidussi prove NP-completeness for 4-regular Hamiltonian graphs in which the components of the complement of the given Hamiltonian cycle are non-selfcrossing cycles of fixed constant length at least four.
source_backed_hard_boundary.firewall: The accessible abstract establishes this fixed-length-at-least-four source class. This artifact does not strengthen that citation to a standalone claim that the C4-only subclass is NP-complete unless separately sourced.
source_backed_hard_boundary.parameter_note: Smooth 4-regular Hamiltonian 3-colourability is FPT in the number r of inner cycles, but fixed-length hard sources have r=Theta(n), so this does not yield a polynomial worst-case route.

positive: A sharp local witness emerges immediately beyond the triangle terminal: one binary diagonal equality per C4.
The C4-only subclass has a polynomial-size two-choice contraction representation with exact witness lifting.
This supplies a new structured target for Hamiltonian/global cancellation methods rather than generic 3-COLOR.
anti_loop: Do not branch independently on all C4 diagonals; that is 2^r and is exponential when r=Theta(n).
Do not infer that every C4-only graph is 3-colourable; the frozen 8-vertex control is an explicit counterexample.
Do not claim C4-only NP-completeness from the broader fixed-length source statement without a separate source.

next_target.name: E8_C4_DIAGONAL_SWITCH_GLOBAL_CONTRACTION_V5_4
next_target.directive: Seek a polynomial operation that correlates many C4 diagonal witnesses at once. Work in either the quotient-colouring view or the equivalent GF(3) tension/interval view. A successful rule must avoid 2^r diagonal branching, preserve exact 3-colourability and reconstruct both diagonal witnesses and colours in polynomial time.

sources: H. Fleischner and M. Stiebitz, A solution to a colouring problem of P. Erdos, Discrete Mathematics 101 (1992), 39-48.
H. Fleischner and G. Sabidussi, 3-colorability of 4-regular hamiltonian graphs, Journal of Graph Theory 42(2) (2003), 125-140.
E. Mujuni, Parameterized Algorithms in Smooth 4-Regular Hamiltonian Graphs, Mathematics in Computer Science 1(4) (2008), 701-708.
